findings.title: architecture.md omits link delivery semantics
findings.problem: The spec requires README and architecture.md to state link semantics (same switch, already opted-in servers gain link reading on deploy, stdio proxy trust sentence, link read after the file is complete). architecture.md only gained MCP_CONNECT_EXPORT_* env rows (lines 232-236); README carries all points.
findings.impact: Required spec documentation criterion is partial; operators reading the architecture guide miss that existing opted-in servers now get link resolution on deploy.
findings.recommendation: Add the link semantics to the file-export section of architecture.md, mirroring the README wording.

findings.title: Apply-level dup link outcome is untested
findings.problem: In _export_call a LinkOutcome of kind 'dup' falls through both branches, so the resource_link is removed with no replacement. Only collect_exports outcomes are asserted (test_link_to_delivered_path_is_dup, test_two_links_to_one_path_give_one_item); no apply/route test covers an explicit path plus a link to it, or two links to one path.
findings.impact: A regression that leaves the raw resource_link, emits a note or double-attaches the file would pass every current test, and the README promise ships unverified at the response boundary.
findings.recommendation: Add apply-level tests: write a.txt, call export.apply(_ctx(['a.txt']), _linked(_link(root / 'a.txt')), {}) and assert content is the two text items plus one resource a.txt (no resource_link, no note, no second chip); likewise two links to one path give exactly one resource at the first link position.
findings.check_notes: apply-level tests added for explicit path plus link and two links to one path

fix.change: added apply-level tests for explicit-path+link and two-links-one-path

findings.title: L3 normalisation test lacks outcome assertions
findings.problem: Spec L3 requires, per SDK-built ResourceLink form, the observed normalised string AND the resulting outcome. TestAnyUrlNormalisation.test_sdk_link_dump asserts only the dumped string; test_raw_dict_link_keeps_exact_string checks one form and opens with a tautology (raw['uri'] == uri). Accepted-after-normalisation cases such as file://localhost/... are unasserted, while the raw-dict TestExtractLinks refuses them.
findings.impact: Production feeds extract_links the SDK-normalised string, so what it actually accepts or refuses per form is unverified; a change in AnyUrl normalisation or _link_path would go unnoticed.
findings.recommendation: For each form assert the extract_links outcome of the normalised string (accepted path or refusal reason) alongside the dumped string; keep raw-dict refusal cases for every form and remove the tautological assertion.
findings.check_notes: CASES carry sdk and raw outcomes, asserted via extract_links; tautology removed; reason strings match export.py constants

fix.change: normalisation table now asserts extract_links outcome for SDK-dumped and raw-dict strings per form; removed tautology

findings.title: Commit subjects exceed 72 characters
findings.problem: development-practices.md documents EPMCDME-xxx: subjects under 72 chars; 8 of 16 branch commits exceed it (73 to 101 chars), including 'Fix export review findings (trailing-slash name, budget release on error, cancel test)' (101) and 'Add explicit file export module with prepare/apply hooks in /bridge' (82), which also packs unrelated fixes.
findings.impact: Breaks the documented commit-format standard and the one-logical-change rule in git-workflow.md.
findings.recommendation: Shorten subjects to under 72 chars (e.g. 'EPMCDME-14735: Fix export review findings') with detail in the body; the MR is squash-merged, so the squash subject can carry the fix.
findings.check_notes: Command record bound to HEAD, exit 0; reflog shows filter-branch rewrite; count result self-asserted, not independently verified
